name: Antijuan Wilkes Jr.
strengths: Wilkes gets immediate depth on the kickslide as Cass Tech LT #52 and uses length to keep edge rushers off his chest while staying square.
Wilkes climbs to the second level on pulls and gets out in space — functional lateral movement for a 6-5 tackle sealing the off-ball LB.
Wilkes finishes through the whistle at the point of attack and works to sustain blocks once engaged.
weaknesses: Wilkes still needs more functional mass and consistent pad level to sit vs power — frame is projectable, anchor is the growth item.
comparison: Wilkes comps to Kelvin Banks Jr. — 6-4/6-5 tackle mold with length and foot quickness who wins early with kickslide depth and second-level mobility before the mass fully arrives.
projection: Wilkes projects as develop Year 1 in the tackle room, then Year 2–3 compete for an SEC starting tackle job — multi-year left tackle ceiling as the long Cass Tech edge-setter who climbs.
schemeFit: Wilkes fits a zone/gap hybrid tackle who can kickslide with length and still get to the second level in the run game.
